_comment: Single source of truth for the website. Every value below is copied from the manuscript 'Student_performance_perdiction_IEEE_Final.md'. The website must not contain any result number that is not in this file.

paper.title: Use of Machine Learning Techniques and Explainable AI for Predicting Student Performance: An Experimental Study With the Open University Learning Analytics Dataset (OULAD)
paper.affiliation: Department of Computer Science and Engineering, JAIN (Deemed-to-be University), Bengaluru, India
paper.status: Manuscript (journal volume, dates and acceptance fields are still placeholders: XX Month 2026)
paper.scope_statement: Experimental and observational study. Attributions convey predictive association, not causal effects. Subgroup results are descriptive and are not fairness conclusions.

dataset.name: Open University Learning Analytics Dataset (OULAD)
dataset.target: is_at_risk = 1 if Withdrawn or Fail; 0 if Pass or Distinction

models.name: Random Forest
models.params: 200 trees, max_depth=15, min_samples_leaf=10 (as stated in the manuscript)

threshold.rule: max{theta in [0.10, 0.90] : Recall >= 0.82 and Precision >= 0.70}, selected on the validation partition only

shap.caveat: Attributions reflect observational association with model predictions and are not causal.

subgroup_note: Descriptive only. These values do not imply that the model is fair. A dash means the value is not reported in the manuscript.

robustness.seed_statement: Performance was consistent across seeds (no per-seed numbers are reported in the manuscript).
robustness.decision: Unweighted, native probabilities were used for all final test predictions and SHAP explanations.

discussion_points: At theta = 0.45 the model identifies 82.38% of at-risk students while flagging 721 of the 2,307 successful holdout students as at-risk.
Error rates are not uniform across strata and should be monitored in any deployment.
Static intake information was less discriminative than early academic and VLE information.
limitations: OULAD does not come from a traditional campus-based university, so generalizability is not established.
Results are descriptive and do not identify causal effects of interventions.
Fail and Withdrawn are grouped as an operational modeling choice.
The data contain no logs of instructor communication or other private institutional activities.
SHAP explains what drives the model's predictions, not which interventions are effective.

do_not_display.claim: The class-weighted variant added 157 false positives
do_not_display.reason: Inconsistent with the manuscript's own specificity figures: 68.75% to 65.31% on 2,307 successful students implies about 79 extra false positives. Show only the specificity values.
